text:
Alex: Heads-up: I'm experimenting with a different canary split strategy to reduce sample drift for large-traffic endpoints — thinking a Zipf-like weighted splitter instead of pure uniform weights. Wanted feedback on routing/telemetry implications. :thinking:
Maria: Interesting. Is the goal to bias early traffic toward smaller downstream latency tails? Or to preserve representativeness for rare keys?
Alex: Both, actually. For our inference endpoints a tiny portion of requests cause long tails; if we put canary weight evenly, we either overload the canary or under-observe failure modes. Zipf-ish gives heavier weight to high-volume keys while still sampling the long-tail at a low rate.
Cheng: Hmm. How would that interact with header overrides (X-Canary, X-Session-ID) and our existing header-first route precedence? We currently call header matches before weighted splits.
Alex: Proposal: keep header-first precedence for explicit opt-ins, but when matching via weights, compute sample bucket using a combined entropy of session cookie + user-id header when present. That keeps stickiness but avoids header-only routes accidentally hijacking canaries.
Sam: What about retries? If a request fails in canary and retries hit fallback, we don't want double-counting telemetry. Need an idempotency marker or `x-canary-origin` header.
Maria: +1 for an origin header. Also we should add a per-request telemetry field `routing.decided_by` with values {header, weight, fallback, sticky} so dashboards can filter.
Alex: Agreed. Draft gate config (pseudo):
```json
{
  "rule_order": ["header_first", "sticky_bucket", "weighted_split", "fallback"],
  "weighted_split": {
    "algorithm": "zipfian",
    "params": {"s":1.07},
    "seed_src": ["X-User-ID","cookie:sess_id"]
  },
  "header_first": {
    "headers": ["X-Canary","X-Experiment"]
  }
}
```
Cheng: Nice. A couple of guardrails: (1) limit absolute canary qps per host to avoid OOMs, (2) enforce quota fallback with a hard cap and a sampling override flag for emergencies.
Sam: For console UX: we should expose an "expected sample rate" estimate per bucket and a simulated preview mode that shows how 10k requests would distribute across canary/primary. Engineers love seeing numbers before flipping switches.
Maria: Telemetry needs: add `metric.routing.count` with tags: `decided_by`, `candidate`, `final_target`, `reason(fallback|quota|error)`. Also a histogram for `routing.latency.ms`.
deploy-bot: deploy plan created for branch alex/zipf-canary-config (staging only). :robot_face:
Alex: Thanks. Cheng / Maria — can one of you take a quick pass on the config semantics and the metrics names? I can wire up the preview UI once we have the backend hook.
Cheng: I'll take config semantics. Quick note: make sure split determinism across languages (Go/Node/Python) — use fnv64a for bucket hashing.
Maria: I'll own telemetry naming and dashboard panels. Will add a Grafana panel mock and a flux query.
Alex: Sweet. Follow-ups: (1) add `x-canary-origin` to request trace span, (2) add preview API endpoint `/routing/preview` that accepts a sample seed list, (3) add e2e test that simulates heavy-tail traffic to assert canary doesn't burst beyond capacity.
ops-bot: FYI: created incident checklist link /playbooks/canary-overload for runbooks if canary breaches 95th pct latency.
Sam: One more UX ask — add a "graceful-degrade" toggle that automatically halves canary weight on errors for N minutes. That avoids manual rollbacks.
Alex: Good idea. Can we make that TTL-configurable and expose an override for SRE?
Cheng: Yes. I'll include TTL and a manual lock in the config object.
Maria: OK. I'll drop a telemetry proposal PR by EOD with panel mocks.
Alex: Thanks everyone. I'll start wiring the preview API and link the staging deploy. :thumbsup:
